title: Touring today compared with the old road days
summary: Road travel is now more expensive but more pleasant under a considerate tour manager; he recalls $75 a week, paying his own hotel, tipping a valet, and plans to keep traveling.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How do you find being on the road now different than say when you were working on the ...

Well it's a whole lot different. Like in what way? It's a whole lot different in many ways. Like in what way? It's more expensive, but you get, it's convenient, it's much more pleasant than before. Like traveling especially with the Japanese jurisdiction where he's been handling, he's been treating the musicians very nice. So I've traveled on the roads before, I've worked with Miller and I wasn't getting a whole lot of money. But everybody had to hand out like Henry Clay. We had a valet who used to travel with us. He was getting a salary. But anytime you ask him to do something, one of them would figure, I used to play a theater listen, he'd have to do something, he'd expect him something. Like he'd want a sandwich or he'd want your clothes pressed, your shoes shined, things like that. And what you're going to do is $75 a week. Of course they paid the transportation, but you paid your own hotel bill. It was expensive then according to the times. Of course now it's more expensive because you go to one of the hotels and you run anywhere from $35 to $40 a night. And that's a whole lot of expense. And I don't like that. That's the part I really don't like. When we started out it was very nice and you could get a place for $12, $15, you know, sometimes $9 or $10 and they had some places, they advertised they'd spare $6. You get that in the moment. It was very nice, I enjoyed it. In fact I like playing music. I've done a whole lot for nothing so now I'm able to get a little money. I've been doing a lot.
Do you think you'll keep on traveling a lot?
As long as I'm able to walk I guess, I think they'll still want me. They could do without me though I guess, you know, for a dime. Yeah. Yeah.
